model.name: QLM score (Quality - Liquidity - Money)
model.purpose: Ranks the qualifying events by how tradeable and how quickly resolvable they are. It is a ranking heuristic built only from official API fields. It is not a probability of winning, it is not a price forecast, and it does not assert a cause for any move.
model.formula: score = 100 x SUM(weight x normalised component) / SUM(weight of available components)

components.move_size: |delta| of the qualifying move, capped at $0.50
components.fee_efficiency: |delta| divided by the round-trip taker fee for a 10-contract clip at the post-move price
components.depth: contracts resting within $0.02 of the post-move price, ranked against the strongest candidate in this snapshot
components.money_behind: measured 24 h traded notional, log-scaled against the strongest candidate in this snapshot
components.horizon: hours to close_time, capped at 720 hours
components.recency: hours since the move, decayed as 1 / (1 + hours / 6.0)

limits: The score ranks tradeable, liquid, fast-resolving candidates. It does not estimate the probability that an event resolves YES.
Realised ROI needs the settlement result (YES pays $1 per contract, NO pays $0) and is tracked separately by the simulation ledger pages.
Depth and traded notional are normalised against the other candidates in this snapshot, so the score is a relative ranking, not an absolute value.
Every input is a demo-environment value; Kalshi states demo prices may not reflect real markets.
